1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module sixteen, the final module: Exam Technique and Final Review. You now know the content. This module is about turning what you know into points. You will learn how to pace the exam, how to read and answer all four question types, how to avoid look-alike traps, and how to use your last week and exam day.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Pace the sixty-five questions in ninety minutes, with checkpoints. Use a four-step method: read, predict, eliminate and confirm. Handle multiple-response, ordering and matching questions, qualifier words and look-alike traps. And plan your final week, exam day and, if needed, a retake.

1.title: Case Check-In: Cedar and Salt's Mock Exam
1.text: At Cedar and Salt Travel, a teammate sat a practice exam and finished just under the pass mark. The review showed lost points, not lost knowledge: misread questions, look-alike services and blank answers. The course content is covered, so now technique has to match it. Your job is to turn what you know into points.

1.title: The Exam Clock
1.text: This slide goes beyond the guide. Sixty-five questions in ninety minutes is about eighty-three seconds each. Aim for about seventy seconds on a first pass, and keep the spare time for the hard questions. Use checkpoints as the latest you should reach: question twenty by minute twenty-eight, question forty by minute fifty-five, and question sixty-five by minute eighty-five. Fifteen questions are unscored, and you cannot tell which, so treat every one as real. Exam tip: if you are behind at a checkpoint, answer quickly and move on, because a blank always scores zero.

1.title: Read for the Requirement
1.text: This slide goes beyond the guide. Read the last line first, because it holds what is being asked; that is a tip from A W S's own certification blog. Then read the scenario and underline the requirement words: most cost-effective, least operational overhead, most secure, quickest to build. Note the verb: filter, detect, explain, ground, evaluate, audit or encrypt. Note the subject: the model, the data, the prompt, the agent or the account. And predict the answer before you look at the options. Exam tip: the scenario is the story, and the last line is the test.

1.title: A Four-Step Answer Method
1.text: This slide goes beyond the guide as well. The picture shows four steps for every question. Read: the last line first, then the scenario. Predict: name the service or idea before you see the options. Eliminate: remove the options that are clearly wrong. And confirm: match the requirement word and the verb to what is left. Exam tip: a prediction stops a plausible distractor from pulling you off course.

1.title: Eliminating Distractors
1.text: Distractors are real services and ideas that sound plausible, so ask why each one fails. Wrong job: it does something else; Guardrails filters, and Clarify finds bias. Wrong effort: fine-tuning or pre-training when a prompt or R A G would do. Wrong tool: SageMaker A I when Bedrock needs less effort, or the reverse. Half true: one clause fits and another does not. And words such as always and never deserve a second look. Exam tip: remove two of four options and a guess is right half the time.

1.title: Multiple-Response Questions
1.text: A multiple-response question has two or more correct answers among five or more options. The question tells you how many to choose, such as, select two. The exam guide says you must select all correct responses to receive credit. So judge each option on its own, true or false against the question, and then count. Choose exactly the number asked. Exam tip: if three options fit, reread the question for the word that rules one out.

1.title: Ordering and Matching Questions
1.text: This exam also has ordering and matching questions. In an ordering question, you get a list of three to five responses to complete a task, and you select them and place them in order. Find the first and last steps, then fill the middle. In a matching question, you match a list of responses to three to seven prompts, and you must match all pairs correctly. Start with the pairs you are sure of; the rest get easier. Both are all or nothing, per the guide, so check every position before you move on. Exam tip: know the order of the lifecycles and the one-line job of each service.

1.title: Qualifier Words Steer the Answer
1.text: Qualifier words steer the answer. Most cost-effective: a smaller model, prompt engineering or R A G before tuning, batch for jobs that can wait, and on-demand for spiky use. Least operational overhead: managed services, such as Bedrock, Knowledge Bases and Guardrails. Most control: SageMaker A I and your own models. Current or private data: R A G with a knowledge base. Consistent answers: a low temperature. Least privilege and most secure: I A M roles, K M S, PrivateLink and narrow permissions. And explain or document: an explainable model, Model Cards and source citation. Exam tip: underline the qualifier, because it picks one correct answer from several that work.

1.title: Generative AI Question Shortcuts
1.text: Many questions are symptom-to-fix patterns. Invented facts: R A G grounding and a contextual grounding check. Different answers to the same prompt: nondeterminism, so lower the temperature. Harmful content or personal data: Guardrails filters. A task skill from labeled examples: fine-tuning. Jargon from unlabeled text: domain adaptation, or continued pre-training. A big model that costs too much: distillation, or a smaller model. Repeated long context: prompt caching. And who did it, or what changed: CloudTrail, or Config. Exam tip: most questions are pattern matching, so name the symptom first, then the fix.

1.title: When You Are Unsure
1.text: When you are unsure, never leave a question blank. The exam guide says an unanswered question counts as incorrect, and a guess has no penalty. Eliminate first, then choose between what is left. When two answers fit, prefer the one that is managed, least privilege and simplest. This is a foundational exam, so answers that need coding, tuning or building pipelines are less likely. Change an answer only when you find a specific reason. And if the screen lets you mark a question to revisit, use it for hard ones, and check the exam tutorial. Exam tip: a blank always scores zero, and a guess might not.

2.title: Your Final Week
2.text: Plan your final week. Seven days out, read the current exam guide again and check for changes. Six to four days out, redo the questions for your two weakest domains, and write your own look-alike notes. Three days out, take a timed run of about sixty-five questions in ninety minutes; A W S offers free practice question sets. Two days out, read Module fifteen once, then say the lists aloud. The day before, do a light review, get a good night's sleep and sort out your exam-day logistics. Exam tip: practice under the clock, because pace is a skill that improves with repetition.

2.title: Exam Day and Afterwards
2.text: Now exam day and afterwards. You can take the exam at a Pearson V U E test center, or online with a proctor; read the provider's rules for identification, room and check-in. The fee is one hundred U S dollars, and a pass is valid for three years. Results are posted to your A W S Certification Account within five business days after the exam, unless held for review. If you do not pass, wait fourteen calendar days; there is no limit on attempts, and each one needs the full fee. If you pass, you cannot retake the same exam for two years. As of five November twenty twenty-six, A W S may change fees and policies, so read its pages before you book. Exam tip: policies and fees change, so check A W S's certification pages before you book.

2.title: Design Check: Cedar and Salt's Mock Exam
2.text: Now a design check. Cover the right column and name the technique. Ran short of time in the last ten questions: use checkpoints, question twenty by minute twenty-eight, and forty by minute fifty-five. Chose fine-tuning for quickest and cheapest: read the qualifier, because prompts or R A G come first. Picked one answer in a, select two, question: judge each option and choose exactly two. Put lifecycle steps in the wrong order: anchor the first and last steps, then fill the middle. Left three questions blank: answer every one, since there is no penalty. And chose Clarify to filter harmful output: read the verb, because filtering is Guardrails. Pause the video if you want more time.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Pace: sixty-five questions, ninety minutes, about eighty-three seconds each, with checkpoints. Method: read the last line, predict, eliminate, confirm. Types: multiple choice, multiple response, ordering and matching, with all-or-nothing credit on the last three. Traps: look-alike services, qualifier words and absolute words. When unsure, never leave a blank, because there is no penalty for guessing. And plan a final week, exam day and, if needed, a retake after fourteen days.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Cedar and Salt wants a chatbot to answer from policy documents that change every week, with the least operational overhead. Which solution fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, which provides managed R A G. The requirement words are current documents and least operational overhead. Updating the data source is enough. Pre-training and fine-tuning cost time and money every week, and self-hosting adds operations.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Cedar and Salt wants to keep Amazon Bedrock traffic private and limit who can call a model. Which two actions help? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C. A W S PrivateLink keeps traffic off the internet, and I A M roles with narrow policies limit who can call a model. Shared keys, open endpoint policies and disabled logging weaken security.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Cedar and Salt's assistant performs well overall but poorly for guests who write in one language. What is the best first step? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: compare the results by language group, which is subgroup analysis. Unequal results across groups point to bias, and subgroup analysis shows where the gap is. Then improve the data, add representative examples and monitor.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. With six minutes left, a candidate has four questions unanswered and is unsure of each. Based on the exam guide's scoring rules, what should they do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: answer all four, since a blank scores zero and a guess has no penalty. The exam guide says unanswered questions are scored as incorrect. A guess can only help.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Auditors ask Cedar and Salt for A W S's compliance reports and for the history of changes to its resource configurations. Which two services fit? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C. A W S Artifact provides on-demand compliance reports, and A W S Config records resource configuration and its history. Macie finds sensitive data, Polly is text to speech, and Inspector scans workloads for vulnerabilities.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all five answers. Question one: B. Question two: A and C. Question three: D. Question four: A. Question five: A and C. That completes the course. You have covered all five domains and fourteen task statements. Read the current exam guide once more, practice under the clock, and good luck with your exam.
